title: Thai Green Curry Lentil Soup
ingredients: 1 (4-oz) package sliced mixed mushrooms (cremini, oyster, shiitake)
1 (1-inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped (about 2 Tbsp)
2 large garlic cloves, finely chopped (about 1 Tbsp)
1 bunch scallions, dark greens separated from white and light green, thinly sliced
1/4 cup green curry paste (Maesri or similar)
2 cups peeled butternut squash, 1/2-inch chop (about 12 oz)
1 bunch fresh cilantro with tender stems, coarsely chopped, plus more to garnish
1 tsp fish sauce (Red Boat or similar)
Thinly sliced Fresno chile, to garnish
steps: Heat the oil in a medium Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave them alone until browned on one side, 3-4 min. Stir and keep cooking until tender, about 2 min more.

Add the ginger, garlic, and the white and light green scallion, stirring constantly until fragrant, about 1 min. Stir in the curry paste and cook, stirring, 1 min more - blooming it in the oil is what deepens the broth.
Add the broth and squash. Bring to a boil, then drop to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the squash is tender, 10-12 min.
While it simmers: set aside 1/4 cup of the coconut milk for drizzling. Put the rest in a blender with the cilantro, miso and scallion greens. Blend smooth, about 30 seconds.

Stir the lentils into the pot, breaking up any clumps. Add the fish sauce, salt, and the blended coconut mixture. Cook over medium, stirring often, just until warmed through, about 2 min - no longer, or the green fades.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with the reserved coconut milk, and top with Fresno chile and more cilantro. Lime wedges at the table.
notes: Lentil swaps: cooked French green lentils are closest - they hold their shape like black lentils. Brown or green work but go softer. Skip red lentils, they dissolve. Frozen butternut is fine straight from frozen; it softens faster and releases water, so start checking early. Mushrooms: spread them out and do not stir for the first few minutes or they steam instead of browning. Green curry pastes vary a lot in heat and salt - taste before the final seasoning. Vegetarian: use vegetable broth and skip the fish sauce (add a little extra miso or salt). Serve as-is, or over steamed jasmine rice for a bigger dinner.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes (Half / Full / 2x)
ingredients: Butter, melted and cooled - 2 Tbsp | 4 Tbsp | 1 stick (8 Tbsp)
Butter or neutral oil for the pan
steps: Whisk the dry ingredients together in a large bowl: flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt.
In a second bowl whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the wet into the dry and stir with a fork just until no dry flour remains. Lumps are correct - do not beat it smooth.
Rest the batter 10 min while the pan heats. It will thicken and puff slightly.
Heat a nonstick skillet or griddle over medium. Film with butter or oil and wipe off the excess.
Scoop 1/4 cup per pancake. Cook until bubbles form across the surface and the edges look dry, 2-3 min.
Flip once and cook 1-2 min more, until the second side is golden and the center springs back.
Hold finished pancakes on a rack in a 200F oven; stacking on a plate steams them soft.
notes: HALF makes about 6 four-inch pancakes (2 people). FULL makes about 12 (4 people). 2x makes about 24 - use two pans or a griddle, and expect to re-butter every other batch. No buttermilk: per 1 cup milk, stir in 1 Tbsp lemon juice or white vinegar and let sit 10 min. Batter keeps covered in the fridge 1 day; it loses some lift, so add a pinch more baking powder when you use it. Cooked pancakes freeze well - cool flat, freeze on a sheet, then bag; reheat in the toaster.
